title: Power Sets and Cartesian Products
short: A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets, and A × B has |A| · |B| ordered pairs.
trouble: Students leave ∅ and the whole set out of the list of subsets, or treat the ordered pair (a, b) as the set {a, b}.

blocks.html: Two ways of building new sets come up constantly in counting and in the study of relations. Both start from the set operations you know, and both have sizes you can find without listing.

The power set $\mathcal{P}(A)$ is the set of all subsets of $A$; if $|A| = n$, then $|\mathcal{P}(A)| = 2^{n}$. The Cartesian product $A \times B$ is the set of all ordered pairs $(a, b)$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$; $|A \times B| = |A| \cdot |B|$.

To build a subset of $A$, go through the elements one at a time and decide "in" or "out." That is $n$ independent two-way choices, so $2^{n}$ subsets, and the choices "all out" and "all in" give $\varnothing$ and $A$ itself. To build a pair, choose the first entry ($|A|$ ways) and then the second ($|B|$ ways). Order matters in a pair: $(1, 2) \ne (2, 1)$, while $\{1, 2\} = \{2, 1\}$. That is the whole point of a pair: it records which entry came first.

blocks.title: Products in both orders
blocks.q: Let $A = \{1, 2\}$ and $B = \{x, y, z\}$. List $A \times B$. Is $A \times B = B \times A$?
steps: $B \times A$ contains $(x, 1)$, whose first entry comes from $B$. That pair is not in $A \times B$.
So $A \times B \ne B \times A$, even though both have $6$ elements.

blocks.title: Counting subsets with a condition
blocks.q: How many subsets of $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$ contain $1$ but not $2$?
steps: The decisions for $1$ and $2$ are forced: $1$ in, $2$ out.
The other $4$ elements are free: $2^{4} = 16$ subsets.

blocks.html: Leaving out $\varnothing$ and the whole set, or treating a pair as a set. A list of the subsets of $\{a, b\}$ that has only $\{a\}$ and $\{b\}$ is missing two: $\varnothing$ and $\{a, b\}$. And $(a, b)$ is not $\{a, b\}$: the pair $(3, 3)$ is fine, but the set $\{3, 3\}$ is just $\{3\}$. Check: your count of subsets must be $2^{n}$, and your count of pairs $|A| \cdot |B|$.
